Module 1.title: DC Circuit Analysis and Network Theorems
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: DC Circuits & Theorems
  • Kirchhoff's Laws: KCL ($\sum I_{node} = 0$, charge conservation) and KVL ($\sum V_{loop} = 0$, energy conservation).
  • Thevenin's Theorem: Any linear two-terminal active network can be replaced by equivalent voltage source $V_{th}$ in series with $R_{th}$.
  • Norton's Theorem: Equivalent current source $I_N = V_{th} / R_{th}$ in parallel with $R_N = R_{th}$.
  • Maximum Power Transfer Theorem: Maximum power delivered to load when $R_L = R_{th}$ ($P_{max} = \frac{V_{th}^2}{4 R_{th}}$, efficiency $\eta = 50\%$).

Module 2.title: Single Phase and Three Phase AC Circuits
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: AC Circuits
  • RMS and Average Values: For sinusoidal waveform: $V_{rms} = V_m / \sqrt{2} \approx 0.707 V_m$, $V_{avg} = 2 V_m / \pi \approx 0.637 V_m$. Form factor $FF = 1.11$, Peak factor $PF = 1.414$.
  • RLC Series Resonance: Resonant frequency $\omega_0 = 1 / \sqrt{L C}$ ($f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{LC}}$). Current is maximum, power factor $\cos \phi = 1.0$. Quality factor $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{\omega_0 C R}$.
  • 3-Phase Star ($Y$) Connection: $V_L = \sqrt{3} V_{ph}$, $I_L = I_{ph}$. Neutral wire carries zero current for balanced load.
  • 3-Phase Delta ($\Delta$) Connection: $V_L = V_{ph}$, $I_L = \sqrt{3} I_{ph}$.
  • Total 3-Phase Power: $P = \sqrt{3} V_L I_L \cos \phi = 3 V_{ph} I_{ph} \cos \phi$.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Module 2 Reference: AC Fundamentals

Module 3.title: Magnetic Circuits and Single Phase Transformers
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Transformers
  • Magnetic Circuit: Magnetomotive force $\text{MMF} = N I$. Reluctance $\mathcal{S} = \frac{l}{\mu A}$. Flux $\Phi = \frac{\text{MMF}}{\mathcal{S}}$.
  • Transformer EMF Equation: $E_1 = 4.44 f N_1 \Phi_m$, $E_2 = 4.44 f N_2 \Phi_m$. Transformation ratio $K = \frac{N_2}{N_1} = \frac{E_2}{E_1} = \frac{I_1}{I_2}$.
  • Equivalent Circuit & Tests:
    • Open Circuit (OC) Test (rated voltage on LV, HV open): Measures core iron loss $W_i = W_h + W_e$.
    • Short Circuit (SC) Test (rated current through HV, LV shorted): Measures full-load copper loss $W_{cu} = I^2 R_{eq}$.
  • Condition for Maximum Efficiency: Variable copper loss equals constant core iron loss ($W_{cu} = W_i$).

Module 4.title: DC Machines: Generators and Motors
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: DC Machines
  • Generated EMF: $E_g = \frac{\Phi Z N P}{60 A}$ (Lap winding $A = P$, Wave winding $A = 2$).
  • DC Motor Torque: $T = \frac{\Phi Z I_a P}{2\pi A} \propto \Phi I_a$. Back EMF $E_b = V - I_a R_a$. Motor speed $N \propto \frac{E_b}{\Phi}$.
  • DC Series Motor: High starting torque ($T \propto I_a^2$). Danger: Never start on no-load (speed runs dangerously high). Used in electric traction, cranes, hoists.
  • DC Shunt Motor: Nearly constant speed characteristic. Used in machine tools, lathes, centrifugal pumps.

Module 5.title: Three Phase Induction Motors and Electrical Safety
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Induction Motors & Safety
  • Synchronous Speed: $N_s = \frac{120 f}{P}$. Slip $s = \frac{N_s - N}{N_s}$. Rotor frequency $f_r = s f$.
  • Rotor Torque: $T \propto \frac{s E_2^2 R_2}{R_2^2 + (s X_2)^2}$. Condition for maximum torque: $R_2 = s_{max} X_2 \implies s_{max} = R_2 / X_2$. Maximum torque is independent of rotor resistance.
  • Earthing: Connecting metallic non-current carrying parts of equipment to earth to prevent fatal electric shocks ($R_{earth} < 1 - 5\,\Omega$).
  • MCB vs ELCB/RCCB: MCB protects against overloads and short circuits; RCCB detects ground leakage current ($>30\,\text{mA}$) to prevent human electrocution.
